data.content_ref: inline:SRC_003 misattributes the reliability gain to Wisdom of the Crowd / Condorcet aggregation and treats the checklist as merely a 'coordinate system,' which directly undermines the problem's target comparison. The problem asks whether trained non-experts following an explicit checklist beat a single expert; SRC_003's own countercondition concedes the panel loses if the expert's accuracy is much higher (e.g., >0.9 vs 0.6), and Condorcet aggregation requires independent >0.5 judgments—a condition the checklist's common framing may violate (shared framing induces correlated errors). More critically, it does not identify single-evaluation evidence separating genuine reliability gain from mere compliance: aggregation statistics cannot be observed within one evaluation, so the proposed mechanism cannot diagnose the distinction the problem demands.
